handback.title: Opt in: Dokima approves and merges its own pull requests
handback.summary: A repo can opt in so Dokima approves and merges its own pull requests once review and checks pass.
handback.user_story: Owners who opt in see finished pull requests merge on their own, with a note saying why.

acceptance_criteria.text: When auto approve is on, a pull request whose code review and checks passed merges with no person waited on.
acceptance_criteria.words: When it is on, a pull request δokima built is approved and queued by δokima itself as soon as its code review has passed and the required checks (`gates.required`) are green. No person is waited on.

edge_cases.case: A branch behind main merges only at the head brought up to date and green.
With the setting off, nothing merges by itself.

acceptance_criteria.text: When Dokima approves, the pull request gets one line naming the code review record and the green checks.
acceptance_criteria.words: The approval is visibly δokima's (its bot), with a one-line comment naming the code review record and the green checks, so the owner can read it afterwards.

edge_cases.case: With the setting off, no such line is posted.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the code review blocks, the pull request is never approved, even with auto approve on.
acceptance_criteria.words: a PR whose review blocked or whose checks are red is never approved.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The one case is the blocking review; an approving review is tested beside it.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a required check is red, the pull request is never approved, even with auto approve on.
acceptance_criteria.words: a PR whose review blocked or whose checks are red is never approved.

edge_cases.case: A check green before but red once brought up to date with main.

acceptance_criteria.text: Auto approve is off by default, so a passed merge gate still waits for the owner's approval.
acceptance_criteria.words: Add an opt-in setting, off by default, e.g. `merge.auto_approve: true`

edge_cases.case: A repo with no settings file at all.

acceptance_criteria.text: A repo setting owner approval itself still fails as locked; turning auto approve on is the opt-in.
acceptance_criteria.words: `integrity.owner_approval` stays locked for repos that do not opt in; turning on `merge.auto_approve` is the explicit opt-in.

edge_cases.case: A settings file setting both owner approval and auto approve.

acceptance_criteria.text: With auto approve on, the audit says in one line which review blocks the bot, and how to fix it.
acceptance_criteria.words: The audit reports, in one line, when branch protection still requires a human or code-owner review that the bot's approval cannot satisfy, and says what to change

edge_cases.case: The app is already on main's review exemption, so no line is written.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the owner turns auto approve on through setup, setup lets the bot bypass main's required review.
acceptance_criteria.words: Setup can apply that change when the owner turns the setting on.

edge_cases.case: GitHub refuses the change for lack of admin rights; setup fails showing GitHub's reason.

raises.label: Doubt: bot cannot approve
raises.text: The bot cannot approve pull requests it opened. Should its one-line note count as approval? The plan assumes so.
raises.evidence: `agent.yml` opens every pull request with the app's key; GitHub refuses an author's own approval.

raises.label: Two readings
raises.text: Should opted-in repos also be refused setting owner approval directly? The plan assumes yes.
raises.evidence: The issue says it stays locked for repos that do not opt in.

raises.label: Rules: bot never approves
raises.text: Once this lands, the identity rules still say the bot can never approve.
